quote.text: we do not suddenly fall on death, but advance towards it by slight degrees; we die every day. For every day a little of our life is taken from us; even when we are growing, our life is on the wane. We lose our childhood, then our boyhood, and then our youth. Counting even yesterday, all past time is lost time; the very day which we are now spending is shared between ourselves and death. It is not the last drop that empties the water-clock, but all that which previously has flowed out; similarly, the final hour when we cease to exist does not of itself bring death; it merely of itself completes the death-process.
quote.author: Seneca
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Each day with your children is a sliver of precious time; like the slow flow of the water-clock, every moment spent nurturing young minds is an investment in their growth and your legacy as a parent.
    • Recognize that life transitions—from the innocence of childhood to the responsibilities of adulthood—are subtle yet profound; cherish these changes, using each day to instill values and wisdom that will guide them even as time marches on.
  • Leadership:
    • In leadership, every small decision contributes incrementally to either the strength or the erosion of your team’s spirit; be mindful that consistent, virtuous actions build long-lasting influence, much like the persistent passage of time shapes our destiny.
    • Understanding that death (or decline) comes gradually reminds a leader to address minor issues immediately—recognition of the inevitable flow encourages the cultivation of resilience, accountability, and timely change to preserve your legacy.
  • Product Management:
    • Every product, like a life, evolves gradually; small iterations and continuous improvements determine its success, emphasizing that missed opportunities for refinement can eventually accumulate into its undoing.
    • This wisdom teaches product managers to value the incremental—each update, feedback, and feature enhancement contributes to the overall vitality of the product, ensuring that development is a mindful process rather than a sudden overhaul when it’s too late.
